title: A spherical mirror's curvature
hook: Change radius of curvature and predict focal length magnitude.
misconception: focal length magnitude stays fixed when radius of curvature doubles.
objective: Apply f = R/2 to compare focal length magnitude when radius of curvature changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a spherical mirror in the paraxial approximation, f = R/2. When radius of curvature doubles, focal length magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model f = R/2; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a spherical mirror in the paraxial approximation, with a nonzero initial result. If radius of curvature triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on focal length magnitude?
recall.why: Apply f = R/2 under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
